porbos.title: The Night the Call Came • The Roof Opened • The Buraq • Along the Wayside • The Congregation of Prophets at Bayt al-Maqdis • The Mosque Where He Led the Prayer • Two Cups • At the Doors of the Heavens

blocks.1: The last dars ended with the stones of Ta’if. Shoes full of blood. That one word spoken before the angel of the mountains; no. Before that had gone the three-year siege. The hunger-cries of children in the valley had gone. Then Abu Talib had gone, Khadijah (RA) had gone. The outer shield was gone, the home’s solace was gone too. And after that Ta’if; ten days of rejection, the du‘a in the vineyard, a few jinn listening to the Qur’an at Nakhlah on the way back.{{1}}
blocks.2: Today’s event took place about ten years after prophethood; about three years before the Hijrah.{{1}}
blocks.3: But this much can be said. The man whom Ta’if had stoned and driven out, the seven heavens received with honour. The Qur’an speaks of this call in just one verse.
blocks.5: Glorified is that Being who takes His servant overnight from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings I have blessed, to show him some of My signs. Surely He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.{{1}}
blocks.6: One question will stay with us through the whole dars. Five times a day we are called. How many times do we respond at once, and how many times do we say; I will pray in a little while! The answer is at the very far end of that night, where fifty was reduced to five.
blocks.8: The Prophet {{1}} was then in Makkah. Where was he? Two narrations in Sahih al-Bukhari say, in the Hatim of the Ka‘bah, in a state between sleep and wakefulness. In another narration, in his own house; the roof of the house opened. One narration of the Sirah mentions the house of Umm Hani’. Its chain has weakness, and it does not agree with the narrations of Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim; Ibn Kathir has said exactly this. Here the narration of Sahih al-Bukhari 349 is taken; what happened, he himself has told.{{2}}
blocks.10: The roof of my house was opened; I was then in Makkah. Jibril (AS) descended. He split open my chest. He washed it with the water of Zamzam. Then he brought a golden tray filled with wisdom and faith and poured it into my chest. Then he closed the chest. Then he took me by the hand and went up with me to the lowest heaven.{{1}}
blocks.11: A golden tray; inside it faith and wisdom. First the chest was washed, in the water of Zamzam.
blocks.13: Now came the mount. In the description of the Prophet {{1}} it was an animal; white, long, larger than a donkey, smaller than a mule. Its name Buraq.{{2}}
blocks.15: A Buraq was brought to me. A white, long animal; larger than a donkey, smaller than a mule. As far as its sight reaches, there it sets its foot.{{1}}
blocks.16: As far as the eye reaches, there the foot. But it did not let him mount easily.{{1}}
blocks.18: On the night of the Isra’ a Buraq was brought to the Prophet {{1}}; with bridle and saddle. It balked. Jibril (AS) said, do you do this to Muhammad? No one more honoured with Allah has ever mounted your back. Then it was drenched in sweat.{{2}}
blocks.19: A mount with bridle and saddle; and it balked. At the rebuke of Jibril (AS) it was drenched in sweat. Then the Prophet {{1}} mounted its back.
blocks.21: The Buraq ran on. On the way a fragrance came. A scent so sweet that it was not of any flower of this world. The Prophet {{1}} asked Jibril (AS), what is this fragrance?{{2}}
blocks.23: On the night of the Isra’ a fragrance came to me. I said, Jibril (AS), what is this fragrance? He said, the fragrance of the woman who combed the hair of Pharaoh’s daughter and her children. I said, what is her story? He said, one day she was combing the hair of Pharaoh’s daughter, the comb fell from her hand. She said, bismillah. Pharaoh’s daughter said, my father? She said, no; my Lord and the Lord of your father is Allah. The girl said, shall I tell him? She said, tell him. The girl informed Pharaoh. Pharaoh called her and said, do you have a lord other than me? She said, yes; my Lord and your Lord is Allah. Pharaoh had a cow of copper heated, and ordered that she and her children be thrown into it. She said, I have a request of you. Pharaoh said, what? She said, gather my bones and the bones of my children in one cloth and bury us. Pharaoh said, that is your right upon us. Then the children were thrown before her one by one. At last came a suckling infant. It seemed she hesitated on account of him. The infant said, mother, leap in; the punishment of the world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter. Then she leapt.{{1}}
blocks.24: A mother. For the offence of taking the name of Allah in Pharaoh’s court she and her children were thrown into fire. That very fragrance had come on the wind of the road. Going further there was a mound of red sand. There a scene that has no resemblance to the world we know.
blocks.26: I passed by Musa (AS) on the night I was taken on the Isra’, near the red sand mound. He was standing in his grave praying.{{1}}
blocks.27: Standing inside the grave in prayer.{{1}}
blocks.28: Then Jibril (AS) said in three places, get down, pray.{{1}}
blocks.30: Jibril (AS) said, get down, pray. I prayed. He said, do you know where you prayed? You prayed at Taybah; there the Hijrah will take place. Then he said, get down, pray. I prayed. He said, do you know where you prayed? You prayed at Tur Sina’, where Allah spoke with Musa (AS). Then he said, get down, pray. I got down, I prayed. He said, do you know where you prayed? You prayed at Bayt Lahm, where ‘Isa (AS) was born.{{1}}
blocks.31: Taybah; where the Hijrah will later take place. Tur Sina’; where Allah spoke with Musa (AS). Bayt Lahm; where ‘Isa (AS) was born.
blocks.32: The Congregation of Prophets at Bayt al-Maqdis
blocks.33: Then Bayt al-Maqdis. He tied the mount to the ring where the prophets before him used to tie.
blocks.35: I mounted it and reached Bayt al-Maqdis. I tied it to the ring where the prophets used to tie. Then I entered the mosque and prayed two rak‘ahs there.{{1}}
blocks.36: Two rak‘ahs of prayer. Inside the mosque he was not alone. A congregation of prophets was there.
blocks.38: I saw myself among a congregation of prophets. Musa (AS) was standing in prayer; a man of slight build, with curly hair, as if one of the men of Shanu’ah. ‘Isa ibn Maryam was standing in prayer; the one most resembling him is ‘Urwah ibn Mas‘ud al-Thaqafi (RA). Ibrahim (AS) was standing in prayer; the one most resembling him is this companion of yours, that is, the Prophet {{1}} himself. Then the time of prayer came, and I led them in prayer.{{2}}
blocks.39: Musa (AS) standing in prayer. ‘Isa (AS) standing in prayer. Ibrahim (AS) standing in prayer. In speaking of the face of Ibrahim (AS), the Prophet {{1}} named no one. He said, this companion of yours. Himself.
blocks.40: The time of prayer came. Who would be the imam? That decision the Prophet {{1}} did not take himself. Jibril (AS) put him forward.{{2}}
blocks.42: Then I entered Bayt al-Maqdis. The prophets were gathered for me. Jibril (AS) put me forward, and I led them in prayer.{{1}}
blocks.43: The Prophet {{1}} himself said, I led them in prayer. Behind, rows of prophets. In front, one. When the prayer was done, another came before him.
blocks.45: It was said, this is Malik, the keeper of Hell, give him salaam. I turned toward him; it was he who greeted me first.{{1}}
blocks.46: Even the keeper of Hell greeted first.
blocks.47: The Mosque Where He Led the Prayer
blocks.48: Whose the mosque is, how old, that the Prophet {{1}} himself said. Abu Dharr (RA) had asked.{{2}}
blocks.50: I said, O Messenger of Allah, which mosque was established first on earth? He said, al-Masjid al-Haram. I said, then which? He said, al-Masjid al-Aqsa. I said, how many years between the two? He said, forty years. After that, wherever the time of prayer finds you, pray there; for the merit is in that.{{1}}
blocks.51: Al-Masjid al-Haram first. Al-Masjid al-Aqsa after it. Forty years between the two houses. The place where the Prophet {{1}} led the prophets today was the second mosque of the world.
blocks.52: In another hadith of Sahih al-Bukhari, the names of three mosques come together; al-Masjid al-Haram, the Prophet’s Mosque and al-Masjid al-Aqsa.
blocks.54: Preparation for travel (with the intention of reward) may not be made to any place but three mosques; al-Masjid al-Haram, this mosque of the Messenger (the Prophet’s Mosque) and al-Masjid al-Aqsa.{{1}}
blocks.55: Makkah, Madinah, and this Bayt al-Maqdis. And in days ahead, having gone to Madinah, the Prophet {{1}} would pray for sixteen or seventeen months facing this very mosque.{{2}}
blocks.56: Then the qiblah would turn toward the Ka‘bah. That is for the later dars.
blocks.58: After the prayer Jibril (AS) came with two vessels. In one, milk. In the other, wine. It was said, take whichever you wish.{{1}}
blocks.60: Two vessels were brought before me; in one milk, in the other wine. I was told, take whichever of these you wish. I took the milk, and drank. Then it was said, you have found the fitrah, or it was said, you have grasped the fitrah right. Had you taken wine, your ummah would have gone astray.{{1}}
blocks.61: The Prophet {{1}} took the milk. A word came from the mouth of Jibril (AS); fitrah. The simple, right nature of man. And there was one more thing. Had he taken wine the ummah would have lost its way. One person’s one choice, and the fate of a whole ummah tied to it.{{2}}
blocks.62: At the Doors of the Heavens
blocks.63: Now the turn to ascend. In the seven heavens he would meet seven prophets. The order is like this: Adam, ‘Isa and Yahya, Yusuf, Idris, Harun, Musa, at last Ibrahim (peace be upon them).{{1}}
blocks.64: At the door of every heaven the same scene. The door closed. A question from inside. Who? Jibril (AS). Who is with you? Muhammad. Has he been summoned? Yes. Then the door opens. And from inside it is said, welcome to him; what a good arrival! The heavens too have a guardian. In one narration of Bukhari Jibril (AS) says to the keeper of the heaven, open.{{1}}
blocks.66: It was asked, who? He said, Jibril (AS). It was asked, who is with you? It was said, Muhammad. It was asked, has he been summoned? He said, yes. It was said, welcome to him, what a good arrival! Then I came to Adam (AS), greeted him. He said, welcome to you, son and prophet!{{1}}
blocks.69: A man was sitting; on his right some shadows, on his left some shadows. When he looked to his right he laughed, when he looked to his left he wept. He said, welcome, righteous prophet and righteous son! I said to Jibril (AS), who is this? He said, this is Adam (AS), and these shadows on his right and left are the souls of his children. The people on the right are people of Paradise, the shadows on the left are people of Hell. When he looks to his right he laughs, when he looks to his left he weeps.{{1}}
blocks.70: Laughter at the good end of his children. Weeping at the bad end. In the second heaven two maternal cousins; ‘Isa and Yahya (peace be upon them). In the third, Yusuf (AS); in the narration of Muslim he has been given half of beauty.{{1}}
blocks.71: In the fourth, Idris (AS). In the narration of Muslim at this place a word of the Qur’an is cited; Allah has said, he was raised to a high rank.
blocks.73: 56. And mention in the Book Idris. Surely he was a truthful prophet! 57. We raised him to a lofty station.{{1}}
blocks.74: In the fifth, Harun (AS). All gave welcome. All said, prophet and brother. Only Adam and Ibrahim (peace be upon them) said, prophet and son.{{1}}
blocks.75: One a father, one a father’s father. They called him son.

footnotes.0: Summary of the previous dars: Dars 9 (the siege, ‘Am al-Huzn and Ta’if) and its notes (901–927).
footnotes.1: Time of the event: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 2, introduction to Surah Bani Isra’il, p. 219: it is difficult to determine exactly when the Mi‘raj took place; most narrations favour this side, that it took place ten years after receiving prophethood and three years before the Hijrah. Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah (chapter on the Isra’): some said shortly after revelation, some said about ten years after; the second view he called ‘more apparent’.
footnotes.2: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 2, Surah Bani Isra’il 17:1, p. 219 (translation: Tawdih al-Qur’an)
footnotes.3: Location: Sahih al-Bukhari 3207 and 3887 (from Malik ibn Sa‘sa‘ah (RA)): in the Hatim or Hijr, between sleep and wakefulness. Sahih al-Bukhari 349 (from Abu Dharr (RA)): ‘the roof of my house was opened, I was then in Makkah’. From the Sirah: Ibn Ishaq mentions from Umm Hani’, as what reached him (fima balaghahu), ‘ma usriya bi-Rasuli Llahi illa min bayti’ (the Isra’ took place from my house); Ibn Kathir has called the chain weak and reported that according to the narration of the Sahihayn the Isra’ took place from near the Hijr/the mosque (al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, chapter on the Isra’).
footnotes.4: Sahih al-Bukhari 349 (from Abu Dharr (RA); via the chain of Anas ibn Malik (RA))
footnotes.5: Description of the Buraq: Sahih al-Bukhari 3207 and 3887 (from Malik ibn Sa‘sa‘ah (RA)): a white animal, smaller than a mule, larger than a donkey; ‘يَضَعُ خَطْوَهُ عِنْدَ أَقْصَى طَرْفِهِ’ ‘its one step falls at the farthest edge of its sight’.
footnotes.7: The balking of the Buraq: Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 3131 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA)); Imam al-Tirmidhi: hasan gharib. Ibn Ishaq has also said, mursal, from Qatadah, «ثُمَّ قَرَّ حَتَّى رَكِبْتُهُ» ‘then it became still, I mounted its back’ (Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, chapter on the Isra’); only this specific part is mursal, so the talk says only ‘mounted’.
footnotes.8: Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 3131 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA)); Imam al-Tirmidhi: hasan gharib
footnotes.9: The woman who combed the hair of Pharaoh’s daughter: Musnad Ahmad 2821 (from Ibn ‘Abbas (RA)); Shu‘ayb al-Arna’ut: chain hasan; al-Dhahabi: sahih. The story is told on the lips of Jibril (AS).
footnotes.10: Musnad Ahmad 2821 (from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas (RA)); Shu‘ayb al-Arna’ut: chain hasan
footnotes.12: The prayer of Musa (AS): Sahih Muslim 2375 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA)): ‘مَرَرْتُ عَلَى مُوسَى لَيْلَةَ أُسْرِيَ بِي عِنْدَ الْكَثِيبِ الْأَحْمَرِ وَهُوَ قَائِمٌ يُصَلِّي فِي قَبْرِهِ’. The manner of this is not described in the hadith; the dars has added no explanation. The words ‘on the first stretch of the journey’ are said from the general sense of the hadith’s words ‘on the night of the Isra’’; the specific account of place and order is not in the hadith.
footnotes.13: Prayer in three places: Sunan al-Nasa’i 450 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA)): «صَلَّيْتَ بِطَيْبَةَ وَإِلَيْهَا الْمُهَاجَرُ… بِطُورِ سَيْنَاءَ… بِبَيْتِ لَحْمٍ حَيْثُ وُلِدَ عِيسَى»; Zubayr ‘Ali Za’i called it hasan. This account is not in Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim; so as a narration of the hasan level, ‘Taybah’ means Madinah.
footnotes.14: Sunan al-Nasa’i 450 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA)); Zubayr ‘Ali Za’i: hasan
footnotes.17: The imamate and the role of Jibril (AS): Sunan al-Nasa’i 450 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA)): «فَجُمِعَ لِيَ الأَنْبِيَاءُ… فَقَدَّمَنِي جِبْرِيلُ حَتَّى أَمَمْتُهُمْ»; Zubayr ‘Ali Za’i: hasan. Ibn Kathir also wrote, «فَتَقَدَّمَهُمْ إِمَامًا بِهِمْ عَنْ أَمْرِ جِبْرِيلَ» (al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, chapter on the Isra’). In Sahih Muslim 172 there is only ‘the time of prayer came, I led them in prayer’.
footnotes.18: Sunan al-Nasa’i 450 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA)); Zubayr ‘Ali Za’i: hasan
footnotes.20: The first two mosques: Sahih al-Bukhari 3366 and Sahih Muslim 520 (from Abu Dharr (RA)). The forty-year gap between the ‘establishment’ of both mosques has come in the hadith; this dars has not entered the discussion of who built which mosque.
footnotes.21: Sahih al-Bukhari 3366 (from Abu Dharr (RA)); Sahih Muslim 520
footnotes.23: The qiblah: Sahih al-Bukhari 399 (from al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib (RA)): ‘كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ {{1}} صَلَّى نَحْوَ بَيْتِ الْمَقْدِسِ سِتَّةَ عَشَرَ أَوْ سَبْعَةَ عَشَرَ شَهْرًا’ (after the Hijrah to Madinah). This is a topic for the next dars; it is brought here only as a one-line bridge.
footnotes.24: Number of cups: there is variation in the reports. Sahih Muslim 162, 168 and Sahih al-Bukhari 3394, 4709 (at Bayt al-Maqdis, ‘Iliya’): two vessels, wine and milk. Sahih al-Bukhari 3887 (after the matter of Sidrat al-Muntaha): three vessels, wine, milk and honey. A sound source for ‘four’ vessels in this dars could not be verified; so the number has been kept to two and three.
footnotes.25: Sahih Muslim 168 (from Abu Hurayrah (RA)); Sahih al-Bukhari 3394
footnotes.26: Jibril’s (AS) comment: Sahih al-Bukhari 4709 (from Abu Hurayrah (RA)): Jibril (AS), praising Allah, said, ‘[praise be to Allah] who guided you to the fitrah; had you taken wine, your ummah would have gone astray.’
footnotes.27: Questions and answers at the doors of the heavens, and the order: Sahih al-Bukhari 3207 (from Malik ibn Sa‘sa‘ah (RA)): ‘مَنْ هَذَا؟ قَالَ: جِبْرِيلُ. قِيلَ: مَنْ مَعَكَ؟ قَالَ: مُحَمَّدٌ… مَرْحَبًا بِهِ وَلَنِعْمَ الْمَجِيءُ جَاءَ’. The order: in the first heaven Adam, in the second ‘Isa and Yahya, in the third Yusuf, in the fourth Idris, in the fifth Harun, in the sixth Musa, in the seventh Ibrahim (peace be upon them).
footnotes.28: The guardian of the heaven: Sahih al-Bukhari 349 (from Abu Dharr (RA)): ‘قَالَ جِبْرِيلُ لِخَازِنِ السَّمَاءِ: افْتَحْ’ ‘Jibril (AS) said to the khazin (keeper) of the heaven, open’.
footnotes.30: Sahih al-Bukhari 349 (from Abu Dharr (RA); via the chain of Anas ibn Malik (RA))
footnotes.31: Yusuf (AS): Sahih Muslim 162 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA)): ‘إِذَا هُوَ قَدْ أُعْطِيَ شَطْرَ الْحُسْنِ’ ‘he has been given half of beauty’.
footnotes.32: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 2, Surah Maryam 19:56–57, p. 299 (translation: Tawdih al-Qur’an)
footnotes.33: Address: Sahih al-Bukhari 3207: Adam and Ibrahim (peace be upon them) said ‘مَرْحَبًا بِكَ مِنِ ابْنٍ وَنَبِيٍّ’ (welcome, prophet and son); the others ‘مِنْ أَخٍ وَنَبِيٍّ’ (prophet and brother).

quiz.q: According to Tawdih al-Qur’an, when did the Mi‘raj take place?
o: About ten years after prophethood, about three years before the Hijrah
Shortly after receiving prophethood, at the very time the three-year siege began
Sixteen or seventeen months after the Hijrah, when the qiblah changed and facing the Ka‘bah began
Forty years after prophethood, as many years as the gap between the establishment of the two mosques
quiz.e: The exact date is hard to determine; most narrations favour about ten years after.

quiz.q: What was the opening question of the dars?
o: Whether the Mi‘raj happened in a dream or in wakefulness, and what Ibn ‘Abbas’s (RA) explanation is
Why Musa (AS) wept, and what the reckoning of his ummah’s number is
Five times a day we are called; how many times do we respond at once, how many times do we say ‘in a little while’
Who saw Allah, ‘A’ishah (RA) or Ibn ‘Abbas (RA)
quiz.e: The question was put at the start and returned to in the final word.

quiz.q: In what was the chest of the Prophet ﷺ washed on the night of the Mi‘raj?
o: In the water of the Nile, one of the rivers outside the Sidrah
In the water of Zamzam
In the water of the river inside the root of the Sidrah, which flows in Paradise
In the faith and wisdom kept in the golden tray
quiz.e: In the narration of Abu Dharr (RA) the chest is washed in Zamzam; then faith and wisdom are poured in (Sahih al-Bukhari 349).

quiz.q: Which is the description of the Buraq?
o: A grey camel with two sacks on its back
An angel with six hundred wings, seen in his true form
A white animal; larger than a donkey, smaller than a mule
A man of slight build with curly hair
quiz.e: The description of Sahih Muslim 162 and Sahih al-Bukhari 3207.

quiz.q: When the Prophet ﷺ went to mount the Buraq on the night of the Isra’, what happened?
o: The Buraq ran at once, covering the distance by setting its foot at the edge of sight
The Buraq balked; at Jibril’s (AS) rebuke it was drenched in sweat
The Buraq stopped short at a fragrance like that of Pharaoh’s daughter
The Buraq set him down at Taybah and went back
quiz.e: Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 3131 (hasan gharib).

quiz.q: In what state was Musa (AS) seen near the red sand mound on the Isra’ journey?
o: Standing in the sixth heaven, weeping
Leading the prophets at Bayt al-Maqdis
Telling the Prophet ﷺ to go back to reduce the fifty prayers
Standing in his grave, praying
quiz.e: Sahih Muslim 2375 (Anas (RA)).

quiz.q: At the instruction of Jibril (AS), in which three places did the Prophet ﷺ pray on the way of the Isra’ (Sunan al-Nasa’i 450)?
o: al-Masjid al-Haram, the Prophet’s Mosque and al-Masjid al-Aqsa
The red sand mound, Taybah and Tur Sina’
Taybah, Tur Sina’ and Bayt Lahm
Bayt Lahm, the Hatim and Bayt al-Maqdis
quiz.e: Taybah means Madinah, at Tur Sina’ Allah spoke with Musa (AS), at Bayt Lahm ‘Isa (AS) was born.

quiz.q: The fragrance the Prophet ﷺ smelled on the way of the Isra’, in the words of Jibril (AS), is whose?
o: The grave of Musa (AS), where he was praying
The fruit of Sidrat al-Muntaha, which is like the jars of Hajar
The soil of Paradise, which is like musk
The woman who combed the hair of Pharaoh’s daughter and her children
quiz.e: Musnad Ahmad 2821; Shu‘ayb al-Arna’ut: chain hasan.

quiz.q: Who led the prayer in the congregation of prophets at Bayt al-Maqdis?
o: The Prophet ﷺ
Musa (AS), who looked like a man of Shanu’ah
‘Isa (AS), who resembled ‘Urwah ibn Mas‘ud (RA)
Ibrahim (AS), who resembled the Prophet ﷺ
quiz.e: «فَحَانَتِ الصَّلاَةُ فَأَمَمْتُهُمْ» (Sahih Muslim 172).

quiz.q: What does the Prophet ﷺ standing as imam in the congregation of prophets mean in the dars’s words?
o: Rows in front of all the prophets, the last prophet ﷺ behind, as at the doors of the heavens
Rows of all the prophets behind him, the last prophet ﷺ in front
The other prophets behind one prophet, and he was Ibrahim (AS)
At al-Masjid al-Aqsa only two prophets prayed, and one of the two was Musa (AS)
quiz.e: Sahih Muslim 172: «فَأَمَمْتُهُمْ».

quiz.q: How did the Prophet ﷺ become imam in the congregation of prophets (Sunan al-Nasa’i 450)?
o: Musa (AS) left his place and called him forward
Ibrahim (AS) handed him the duty of leading
All stood together and declared him imam
Jibril (AS) put him forward
quiz.e: «فَقَدَّمَنِي جِبْرِيلُ حَتَّى أَمَمْتُهُمْ»; Zubayr ‘Ali Za’i: hasan.

quiz.q: How many years between the first two mosques established on earth?
o: Three years, as the siege lasted
Forty years
Ten years, as the Mi‘raj came after prophethood
Sixteen or seventeen months, as prayer facing Bayt al-Maqdis lasted
quiz.e: In reply to the question of Abu Dharr (RA) (Sahih al-Bukhari 3366).

quiz.q: According to the sound hadith, to which three mosques may one travel with the intention of reward?
o: al-Masjid al-Haram, al-Bayt al-Ma‘mur and al-Masjid al-Aqsa
The Prophet’s Mosque, al-Masjid al-Aqsa and the mosque of the Sidrah
al-Masjid al-Haram, the Prophet’s Mosque and al-Masjid al-Aqsa
al-Masjid al-Haram, the mosque of Ta’if and al-Masjid al-Aqsa
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 1189 (Abu Hurayrah (RA)).

quiz.q: Which piece of information about al-Masjid al-Aqsa in the dars did the Prophet ﷺ himself state?
o: Established before al-Masjid al-Haram, three years between the two
The second mosque of the world after al-Masjid al-Haram, forty years between the two
Established after the Prophet’s Mosque, ten years between the two
Established near the Sidrah, seventy thousand years between the two, and there the Prophet ﷺ led the prophets
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 3366; Sahih Muslim 520.

quiz.q: What was said would happen to the ummah if he took wine?
o: Fifty prayers would have remained on the ummah
The destroying sins would not be forgiven the ummah
The ummah would have entered Paradise fewer than the ummah of Musa (AS)
The ummah would have gone astray
quiz.e: «لَوْ أَخَذْتَ الْخَمْرَ غَوَتْ أُمَّتُكَ» (Sahih Muslim 168).

quiz.q: At the doors of the heavens, which question was asked first from inside?
o: Who? (answer: Jibril (AS))
Who is with you? (answer: Muhammad)
Has he been summoned? (answer: yes)
How is the mosque? (a question of the Quraysh)
quiz.e: The order of the questions in Sahih al-Bukhari 3207 is exactly so.

quiz.q: Which two prophets welcomed the Prophet ﷺ as ‘prophet and son’?
o: ‘Isa and Yahya (peace be upon them), who were maternal cousins
Adam and Ibrahim (peace be upon them)
Musa and Harun (peace be upon them), who were brothers
Yusuf and Idris (peace be upon them), in the third and fourth heavens
quiz.e: In Sahih al-Bukhari 3207 the address of these two is ‘son and prophet’.

quiz.q: Who, and how, was the Prophet ﷺ welcomed at the doors of the heavens?
o: From inside it was said, stop him, he must first give an account
From inside it was said, tell him to get down from the Buraq
From inside it was said, welcome to him, what a good arrival
From inside it was said, tell him to go first to Musa (AS)
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 3207.

porbos.title: Musa’s Weeping • Sidrat al-Muntaha • Whom He Saw • The Question of Seeing • Three Gifts • From Fifty to Five

blocks.1: In the sixth heaven, Musa (AS). Salam was given. He replied. He said, welcome, brother and prophet. Then when the Prophet {{1}} passed beyond him, Musa (AS) wept. Someone asked, why do you weep?
blocks.3: Then I reached Musa (AS). Jibril (AS) said, this is Musa (AS), give him salam. I gave salam, and he replied. Then he said, welcome, righteous brother and righteous prophet. When I passed beyond him, he wept. He was asked, why do you weep? He said, I weep because a young man was sent after me; from his ummah more people will enter Paradise than from my ummah.{{1}}
blocks.4: This is not a weeping of envy. It is the weeping of a prophet. One who struggled with his people all his life, and now sees the followers of a prophet who came after him surpassing his own in number.{{1}}
blocks.6: In the seventh heaven, Ibrahim (AS). In the narration of Muslim, he is sitting with his back against a house.
blocks.8: In the seventh heaven I found Ibrahim (AS); he is leaning his back against al-Bayt al-Ma‘mur. Every day seventy thousand angels enter it; they never return to it.{{1}}
blocks.9: The name of that house is al-Bayt al-Ma‘mur. In the narration of Bukhari there is something more; that house was shown, and a tree.{{1}}
blocks.11: Al-Bayt al-Ma‘mur was raised before me. I asked Jibril (AS). He said, this is al-Bayt al-Ma‘mur; every day seventy thousand angels pray here. Those who go out once never return to it; that is their last turn. Then Sidrat al-Muntaha was raised before me. Its fruits were like the large jars of Hajar, its leaves like the ears of elephants. At its root are four rivers; two inner, two outer. I asked Jibril (AS). He said, the two inner are in Paradise; the two outer are the Nile and the Euphrates.{{1}}
blocks.12: Seventy thousand angels. A new group every day. Those who go out once never come back. Seventy thousand every day; then a fresh seventy thousand again. The rows of worship in the heavens never end.
blocks.13: Then Sidrat al-Muntaha. A lote tree; but what a tree! Fruits like big jars. Leaves like elephants’ ears. And at the root, four rivers. The Qur’an mentions this place in Surah an-Najm.{{1}}
blocks.15: 13. Indeed, he saw him (the angel) another time. 14. Near the Lote-Tree, whose name is Sidrat al-Muntaha. 15. Near it is the Garden of Refuge (Jannat al-Ma’wa). 16. When that which covered the Lote-Tree covered it. 17. The (Messenger’s) eye did not stray, nor did it exceed the limit. 18. The truth is, he saw some of the great signs of his Lord.{{1}}
blocks.16: What covered the tree? The Qur’an says, what was to cover it. And ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud (RA) said, golden butterflies.{{1}}
blocks.17: About the beauty of the Sidrah the Prophet {{1}} himself said something.
blocks.19: Its leaves are like the ears of elephants, its fruits like large jars. When what was to cover it by Allah’s command covered it, it changed. No one of Allah’s creation can describe its beauty.{{1}}
blocks.20: No one can. Then one more scene.
blocks.22: Then I was taken up, until I came to a level ground where I heard the scratching of the pens.{{1}}
blocks.23: He was also made to enter Paradise.{{1}}
blocks.25: Then I was made to enter Paradise. In it were strings of pearls; and its soil was musk.{{1}}
blocks.27: The opening verses of Surah an-Najm show another side of this journey. The matter of seeing someone; twice.
blocks.29: 5. One taught him, a mighty one in power (the angel) 6. who has strength. So he appeared, 7. while he was on the highest horizon. 8. Then he came near and drew down. 9. Until he was at the distance of two bows, or even nearer. 10. Thus Allah revealed to His servant what He had to reveal.{{1}}
blocks.30: What is that true form like? ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud (RA), explaining these verses, said that the Prophet {{1}} saw Jibril (AS), with six hundred wings.
blocks.32: (‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud (RA)) told us that he (the Prophet {{1}}) saw Jibril (AS); he had six hundred wings.{{2}}
blocks.33: An angel of six hundred wings came to a man in human form; with revelation. And the second sighting was on this night of the Mi‘raj, near Sidrat al-Muntaha. Two places of two sightings; the horizon and the Sidrah.
blocks.35: In Surah an-Najm Allah said that the heart of the Prophet {{1}} did not err in what he saw. What did he see?
blocks.37: 11. His heart did not err in what he saw. 12. Will you then dispute with him about what he saw?{{1}}
blocks.38: The first answer of the verses is Jibril (AS); in his true form. The Prophet {{1}} first saw Jibril with the eye, then took him in with the heart. The heart did not err in it.{{2}}
blocks.39: A Tabi‘i went to ‘A’ishah (RA). Masruq. He asked, mother, did Muhammad {{1}} see his Lord?{{2}}
blocks.40: ‘A’ishah (RA) said, what you said made my hair stand on end.
blocks.42: Whoever tells you that Muhammad {{1}} saw his Lord has lied.{{2}}
blocks.43: She gave proof from the Qur’an. And she said, the one the Prophet {{1}} saw is Jibril (AS).
blocks.45: But he saw Jibril (AS) in his true form twice.{{1}}
blocks.46: On this question Salafi scholars hold to the words of ‘A’ishah and Abu Dharr (RA); seeing Allah with the eyes of this world is not established. Abu Dharr (RA) had asked the Prophet {{1}} directly.
blocks.48: I asked the Messenger of Allah {{1}}, did you see your Lord? He said, a light; how could I see Him?{{2}}
blocks.49: The words of Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) have come, that he saw Him with the heart. Salafi scholars take this to mean seeing with the heart; not with the eye.
blocks.51: He saw Him with his heart.{{1}}
blocks.52: Ibn Taymiyyah said, there is no proof for seeing with the eye, and it is not even narrated from any of the Companions.{{1}}
blocks.54: At Sidrat al-Muntaha the Prophet {{1}} was given three things.
blocks.56: When the Messenger of Allah {{1}} was taken on the Isra’, he was brought to Sidrat al-Muntaha; it is in the sixth heaven. What rises up from the earth stops there; it is taken from there. What descends from above also stops there; it is taken from there. Allah said, ‘When that which covered the Lote-Tree covered it’ (Surah an-Najm 16). Ibn Mas‘ud (RA) said, golden butterflies. Then the Messenger of Allah {{2}} was given three things: the five daily prayers, the last verses of Surah al-Baqarah, and, for any of his ummah who did not associate anything with Allah, forgiveness even of the ruinous major sins.{{3}}
blocks.57: One. Five daily prayers. Two. The last verses of Surah al-Baqarah. Three. Forgiveness of the major sins of an ummah who did not commit shirk. The second gift, in the Qur’an’s words, is this.
blocks.59: 285. The Messenger (that is, Hazrat Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace) believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and (so do) the believers (with him). All of them believe in Allah, in His angels, in His books and in His messengers. (They say,) We make no distinction between any of His messengers (that we would believe in some and not in others). And they say, we have heard (the commands of Allah and the Messenger attentively) and we are carrying them out gladly. Our Lord! We beg Your forgiveness, and to You is our return. 286. Allah does not burden anyone beyond their capacity. In their favour is what they do willingly, and against them is what they do willingly. (O Muslims! Make this du‘a to Allah:) Our Lord! Do not hold us to account if we make a mistake or slip. Our Lord! Do not place on us a burden like the one You placed on those before us. Our Lord! Do not load on us what we have no strength to bear. Pardon our faults, forgive us and have mercy on us. You are our Protector and Helper. So help us against the disbelieving people.{{1}}
blocks.60: The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him. The believers too. And they say, we heard and we obeyed. Allah does not burden anyone beyond their capacity. With these verses Surah al-Baqarah ends. In the hadith these very verses are what is called the gift of that night.{{1}}
blocks.61: The third matter is the reward of tawhid. The member of the ummah who, keeping away from shirk, will stand before Allah has a promise of forgiveness even for their ruinous sins.
blocks.63: Now comes the scene for which today’s dars carries its question. Allah made fifty prayers obligatory on the ummah. On the way down, the Prophet {{1}} came to Musa (AS) in the sixth heaven. Musa (AS) asked, what was commanded? Fifty prayers.
blocks.65: Your ummah will not be able to bear fifty prayers. By Allah, I tested people before you, and I tried my utmost with Bani Isra’il. Go back to your Lord.{{1}}
blocks.66: Musa (AS) speaks from his own experience. He had tried his utmost to manage Bani Isra’il. The Prophet {{1}} went back. Allah reduced it. Again he came to Musa (AS). Again the same words. Again going back. Again the reduction.{{2}}
blocks.67: At the end Musa (AS) said again, go back.
blocks.69: I have asked my Lord so much that I have become ashamed. Now I am content, and I submit.{{1}}
blocks.70: Then a call came from above.
blocks.72: Then the call was made: I have put My obligation into effect, I have lightened it for My servants, and I reward a good deed tenfold.{{1}}
blocks.73: And in another narration of Sahih al-Bukhari the matter is even clearer.
blocks.75: I went to Him again. He said, they are five, and they are fifty; the word is not changed with Me. I returned to Musa (AS), and he said, go again to your Lord. I said, I am ashamed before my Lord.{{1}}
blocks.76: In the narration of Sahih Muslim the calculation is stated directly.
blocks.78: O Muhammad, these are five prayers every day and night; ten for each prayer. So that is fifty. Whoever intends a good deed and does not do it, one good deed is written for them; if they do it, ten are written. Whoever intends an evil deed and does not do it, nothing is written; if they do it, one evil is written.{{1}}
blocks.79: Five prayers; five in number, fifty in reward. What Allah Himself made easy, we often find heavy even that.

footnotes.0: Sahih al-Bukhari 3887 (from Malik ibn Sa‘sa‘ah (RA)); Sahih al-Bukhari 3207
footnotes.1: Explanation of the weeping of Musa (AS): the words ‘not envy’ are this dars’s explanation; the hadith’s words are ‘I weep because…’ (Sahih al-Bukhari 3887). In the wording of Sahih al-Bukhari 3207 the word is ‘better than those who will enter Paradise from my ummah’ (أَفْضَلُ); in 3887, ‘أَكْثَرُ’ (more).
footnotes.3: Al-Bayt al-Ma‘mur, the Sidrah and the four rivers: Sahih al-Bukhari 3207 and 3887. Variation in narrations about the location of Sidrat al-Muntaha: in this narration of Sahih al-Bukhari, after the seventh heaven; according to Sahih Muslim 173 (from ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud (RA)), in the sixth heaven. Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 3, note 7 on Surah an-Najm 53:14–15 (p. 431): Sidrat al-Muntaha is a huge lote tree (jujube) of the upper world, near which Paradise is situated.
footnotes.5: Explanation of Surah an-Najm 53:13–18: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 3, note 7 (p. 431): this is the second occasion of seeing Jibril (AS) in his true form, which took place on the journey of the Mi‘raj. Note 8 (p. 432): ‘what covered it’ is beyond description; it is known from hadith that countless angels had then gathered over that tree in the form of golden butterflies. Note 9: the eye was not deceived, nor did it exceed the limit that Allah had set.
footnotes.6: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 3, Surah an-Najm 53:13–18, pp. 431–432 (translation: Tawdih al-Qur’an)
footnotes.7: Golden butterflies: Sahih Muslim 173 (from ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud (RA)): ‘قَالَ فَرَاشٌ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ’ ‘(what covered the tree was) golden butterflies’.
footnotes.9: Sahih al-Bukhari 349 (from Ibn ‘Abbas and Abu Habbah al-Ansari (RA); via Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri)
footnotes.10: Description of Paradise: the word in Sahih al-Bukhari 349 is ‘حَبَايِلُ اللُّؤْلُؤِ’ (strings of pearls); in some narrations ‘جَنَابِذُ اللُّؤْلُؤِ’ (domes of pearl) has come. Here the word of Sahih al-Bukhari 349 has been kept.
footnotes.12: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 3, Surah an-Najm 53:5–10, pp. 430–431 (translation: Tawdih al-Qur’an)
footnotes.14: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 3, Surah an-Najm 53:11–12, p. 431 (translation: Tawdih al-Qur’an)
footnotes.15: Explanation of 53:11: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 3, note 6 (p. 431): that is, it was not that the heart erred in understanding what the eye actually saw; note 7: the second occasion of seeing Jibril (AS) in his true form. Mufti Muhammad Shafi‘, Ma‘ariful Qur’an, Surah an-Najm 53:11: two explanations of these verses are mentioned; one is seeing Jibril in his true form (‘A’ishah, Ibn Mas‘ud, Abu Hurayrah and Abu Dharr (RA)), the other is seeing Allah (Ibn ‘Abbas (RA)); Ma‘ariful Qur’an gives preference to the first view, because the basic meaning of the verb ‘ra’a’ is seeing with the eye and there is no need to take it in a figurative sense.
footnotes.16: Masruq and ‘A’ishah (RA): Sahih al-Bukhari 4855 (from Masruq): ‘I said to ‘A’ishah (RA), mother, did Muhammad {{1}} see his Lord? She said, what you said made my hair stand on end…’. Similar in Sahih Muslim 177.
footnotes.17: Sahih al-Bukhari 4855 (from Masruq, the statement of ‘A’ishah (RA))
footnotes.21: Salafi position: Islam Q&A (fatwa no. 12423): the narration of ‘A’ishah and Abu Dharr (RA) (Sahih al-Bukhari 4855; Sahih Muslim 178); taking Ibn ‘Abbas’s ‘he saw twice’ in the sense of ‘with the heart’; Ibn Taymiyyah: ‘There is no proof for seeing with the eye, and it is not narrated from any of the Companions’; al-Darimi (via Ibn al-Qayyim): ‘the consensus of the Companions that on the night of the Mi‘raj he did not see his Lord’. This is cited as the view of Salafi scholars.
footnotes.23: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 1, Surah al-Baqarah 2:285–286, pp. 166–167 (translation: Tawdih al-Qur’an)
footnotes.24: The third gift: Sahih Muslim 173: ‘وَغُفِرَ لِمَنْ لَمْ يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ أُمَّتِهِ شَيْئًا الْمُقْحِمَاتُ’ (for the member of the ummah who did not associate anything with Allah, the ‘muqhimat’, that is, the major sins that cast one into destruction, are forgiven). Scholars have explanations about the meaning of ‘muqhimat’ and its limits; here it is stated according to the hadith’s word.
footnotes.26: Steps of reduction: according to Sahih al-Bukhari 3207 and 3887, it was reduced by ten each time, finally five. According to Sahih al-Bukhari 349 (from Abu Dharr (RA)), each time by half (‘فَوَضَعَ شَطْرَهَا’), finally five. According to Sahih Muslim 162 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA)), each time by five prayers (فَحَطَّ عَنِّي خَمْسًا). The accounts of the steps in the three narrations differ; the final result is one: five prayers.

quiz.q: Why did Musa (AS) weep?
o: Because fifty prayers had been made obligatory on his ummah, and they would not be able to bear that burden
Because the Prophet ﷺ took milk and put away wine, and so the ummah would find the way
Because more people from the Prophet’s ﷺ ummah would enter Paradise than from his own ummah
Because he had to pray inside the grave, and so had grown tired
quiz.e: The narration of Sahih al-Bukhari 3887.

quiz.q: Why does the dars say the weeping of Musa (AS) is not a weeping of envy?
o: Because he struggled with his people all his life, and sees the followers of the prophet who came after him growing in number
Because he envied the Prophet’s ﷺ prayer, and that weeping also included the count of his ummah
Because he was tired from praying inside the grave
Because he wept thinking of the disobedience of Bani Isra’il
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 3887; the words ‘not envy’ are the dars’s explanation.

quiz.q: In the narration of Ibn Mas‘ud (RA), what covered the Sidrah tree?
o: A colour whose name the Prophet ﷺ does not know
Rows of seventy thousand angels
Strings of pearls and soil of musk
Golden butterflies
quiz.e: Sahih Muslim 173; the mention of colours is in Sahih al-Bukhari 349.

quiz.q: How many wings did Jibril (AS) have, in the narration of Ibn Mas‘ud (RA)?
o: Six hundred
Seventy thousand
Twenty-seven
Forty
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 3232 and 4856.

quiz.q: According to Sahih Muslim 173, which are the three gifts of the Mi‘raj?
o: Five daily prayers, a vessel of milk, and forgiveness of the major sins of an ummah who stayed away from shirk
Five daily prayers, the last verses of Surah al-Baqarah, and forgiveness of the major sins of an ummah free of shirk
Five daily prayers, the last verses of Surah al-Baqarah, and the salam of the angels of al-Bayt al-Ma‘mur
The fruit of the Sidrah, the last verses of Surah al-Baqarah, and forgiveness of the major sins of an ummah free of shirk
quiz.e: «الصَّلَوَاتِ الْخَمْسَ… خَوَاتِيمَ سُورَةِ الْبَقَرَةِ… الْمُقْحِمَاتُ».

quiz.q: What did Allah say in the final call (Sahih al-Bukhari 3207)?
o: If he has said it, then he has spoken truly; I believe him in news even farther than this
I have preferred some prophets over others, and I gave Dawud the Zabur
I put My obligation into effect, I lightened it for My servants, I reward a good deed tenfold
Your companion has not strayed, nor has he erred; he does not speak from his own desire
quiz.e: «أَمْضَيْتُ فَرِيضَتِي وَخَفَّفْتُ عَنْ عِبَادِي وَأَجْزِي الْحَسَنَةَ عَشْرًا».

quiz.q: According to Sahih Muslim 162, what is the calculation by which five prayers are called fifty?
o: Twenty-seven times for each prayer in congregation
Forty times for each prayer prayed on time
Equal to bathing five times a day for the five prayers
Tenfold for each prayer
quiz.e: «لِكُلِّ صَلاَةٍ عَشْرٌ فَذَلِكَ خَمْسُونَ صَلاَةً».

quiz.q: Why did Musa (AS) tell the Prophet ﷺ to go back about the burden on the ummah?
o: Because the Prophet ﷺ had asked him to try to reduce it further
Because Jibril (AS) had told him to ask his Lord
Because hearing the scratching of the pens at the Sidrah, he understood that prayer could be reduced further
From his own hard experience of managing Bani Isra’il
quiz.e: «عَالَجْتُ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ أَشَدَّ الْمُعَالَجَةِ» (Sahih al-Bukhari 3887).

quiz.q: What is the meaning of ‘these are five, and these are fifty’?
o: Five in number, fifty in reward
Fifty in number, five in reward
Five in number, twenty-seven times less
In five prayers, the salam of fifty prophets
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 349.

quiz.q: Which calculation settles ‘five in number, fifty in reward’?
o: Twenty-seven times for each prayer in congregation, so one hundred and thirty-five for the five prayers
The prayer of seventy thousand angels each day, so the same number for the five prayers
Tenfold reward for each prayer, so the reward of fifty in the five prayers themselves
With each prayer the last verses of Surah al-Baqarah, so fifty in five prayers, so the five prayers become equal to the reward of fifty prayers
quiz.e: Sahih Muslim 162: «لِكُلِّ صَلاَةٍ عَشْرٌ فَذَلِكَ خَمْسُونَ».

quiz.q: Why did the Prophet ﷺ go back to Allah again and again?
o: To ask for more time for himself, so that the Buraq could return and Musa (AS) kept saying the same thing again and again
Because Jibril (AS) had told him to go back, to please his Lord
Because the Quraysh were waiting, and he had to return before morning
Because Musa (AS) advised that the ummah could not bear fifty prayers, so for the sake of the ummah
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 3887.

quiz.q: Someone repeatedly delays prayer, saying ‘in a little while’. Which scene of the Mi‘raj is most useful to make them understand?
o: The scene of Adam (AS) laughing on his right and weeping on his left, where the matter of his children’s ends is told
The scene of colour spreading over the Sidrah, which happened by Allah’s command and which no one can describe
The scene of the Buraq placing its foot at the edge of its sight, which shows the speed of the white animal
The scene of fifty being reduced to five on Musa’s (AS) advice, with the reward remaining fifty
quiz.e: «هِيَ خَمْسٌ وَهْيَ خَمْسُونَ» (Sahih al-Bukhari 349).

porbos.title: News at Dawn • The Description of Bayt al-Maqdis • The One Who Said It at Once • Was It a Dream? • The Story of Israel and the End of the Disobedient • The Prophet ﷺ Among the Prophets • Not the Word of One Person • Our Home Today • Final Word

blocks.1: The Prophet {{1}} returned to Makkah within the night. In the morning he was grave, quiet. The worry was that once he told his people, they would call him a liar.{{2}}
blocks.2: A scene that comes after this is in the narration of the Sirah. This much is not in the sound hadith. Abu Jahl saw the Prophet {{1}} and asked, is there any news? The Prophet {{2}} said, yes. Tonight I was taken to Bayt al-Maqdis. Abu Jahl said, Bayt al-Maqdis! Tonight? Yes. Then he asked, if I call your people, will you tell them this very thing just so? The Prophet {{3}} said, yes.{{4}}
blocks.3: Abu Jahl called out, people of Quraysh, come! The Quraysh gathered from their assembly. Abu Jahl said, tell your people what you told me. The Prophet {{1}} told what he had seen. Some clapped. Some whistled.{{2}}
blocks.4: Some of those who had believed earlier turned back.{{1}}
blocks.6: Now the Quraysh’s question came about Bayt al-Maqdis. What is the mosque like? Its doors, its build? Amid so much in the night, not every detail had been kept in the mind of the Prophet {{1}}.
blocks.8: I saw myself in the Hijr, and the Quraysh were asking me about my night journey. They asked me about some matters of Bayt al-Maqdis that I had not retained. I was distressed as I had never been before. Then Allah raised it before me, and I was looking at it. Whatever they asked me, I informed them.{{1}}
blocks.9: One man, the Quraysh all around; question after question. When it came to the details, the Prophet {{1}} was stuck. Inside him was a distress such as he had never had. And just then Allah raised Bayt al-Maqdis before his eyes.
blocks.11: When the Quraysh called me a liar, I stood in the Hijr. Allah revealed Bayt al-Maqdis to me. I began telling them its signs, and I kept looking at it.{{1}}
blocks.12: Questions came, answers came. Questions came, answers came. Those who had seen the mosque could check.{{1}}
blocks.13: Then the Sirah mentions one more proof; of the trade caravans. This is a narration of the Sirah, and its chain has weakness. So it is told as a scene, not as evidence. The Prophet {{1}} said, on the way I saw such-and-such caravan; one of their camels had run away, and I told them its location. When I came to another caravan, the people were asleep; the water in their vessel was covered, I opened the cover and drank the water, and covered it again. And he said, now their caravan is coming down the white pass of Tan‘im; in front is an ash-coloured camel, with two sacks on its back. People ran toward the pass. As had been said, the first camel was that very camel.{{2}}
blocks.14: What is established by a sound chain is the description of Bayt al-Maqdis. And that was enough.
blocks.15: The One Who Said It at Once
blocks.16: Amid this uproar of Makkah, a report went to Abu Bakr (RA). People said to him, have you heard what your companion says?{{1}}
blocks.18: Have you heard about your companion? He claims that tonight he was taken to Bayt al-Maqdis. He said, did he really say this? They said, yes. He said, if he has said this, then he has spoken truly. They said, do you believe him that in one night he went to Bayt al-Maqdis and came back before morning? He said, yes. I believe him in matters even farther than this; I believe him in news of the heaven, morning and evening. For this reason Abu Bakr (RA) was named al-Siddiq.{{1}}
blocks.19: Siddiq means the one who affirms most of all. His logic was simple. The one in whose mouth I have believed the news of the heavens morning and evening, why would I disbelieve a night’s journey from his mouth?
blocks.20: On the very morning when some people were turning away from faith, this sentence came. If he has said it, then he has spoken truly.
blocks.22: Was this journey bodily, in wakefulness? Or in a dream? The question is old. The answer is old too.
blocks.24: And the vision which We showed you, We made only a trial for the disbelievers, and the accursed tree mentioned in the Qur’an.{{1}}
blocks.25: The word in the verse is ‘ru’ya’. In Arabic this word is used both for a dream and for seeing with the eyes. Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) made its meaning clear.
blocks.27: It was a vision of the eye, which was shown to the Messenger of Allah {{1}} on the night when he was taken to Bayt al-Maqdis.{{2}}
blocks.28: In the well-known book of Hanafi creed, al-‘Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, the matter is stated in one sentence.
blocks.30: The Mi‘raj is true. The Prophet {{1}} was taken on the Isra’ and raised with his body, in wakefulness, to the heaven, then to wherever Allah wished of the heights.{{2}}
blocks.31: The Qur’an itself speaks of the eye. Surah an-Najm says, the eye did not stray, nor did it exceed the limit. In a dream, the eye does not see.{{1}}
blocks.32: And the very acts within the event say it was in wakefulness. Riding the Buraq. The Buraq drenched in sweat. Tying the mount at the ring. Two rak‘ahs of prayer. Choosing one of two vessels. Answering the Quraysh’s questions.
blocks.33: Ibn Kathir gave two arguments. First, the verse begins with ‘Subhan’. This word comes before a great, astonishing event. And the verse says ‘His servant’; ‘servant’ means both body and soul. Second, the Quraysh rushed in to call him a liar. If it were a dream, what was the uproar about? Ibn Kathir wrote that this is the view of the majority of the Salaf and Khalaf; with body and soul, in wakefulness.{{1}}
blocks.34: The Story of Israel and the End of the Disobedient
blocks.35: The first verse of Surah al-Isra’ ends speaking of that night. Right after, another matter begins. The matter of Israel.{{1}}
blocks.37: 4. I informed Bani Isra’il in the Book by decree, you will cause corruption on the earth twice and will show great arrogance. 5. So when the first of those two events arrived, I gave dominion over you to servants of Mine who were extremely fierce fighters. They entered your cities and spread out. It was a promise that was bound to be fulfilled.{{1}}
blocks.38: In the first verse, al-Masjid al-Aqsa. In the verses after, the earlier owners of that land. That night the Prophet {{1}} also saw some people whose end was hard.{{2}}
blocks.40: When I was raised up, I passed by a group of people who had nails of copper; they were scratching their faces and chests. I said, O Jibril (AS), who are these? He said, these are those who eat people’s flesh and attack their honour.{{1}}
blocks.41: Backbiting. Eating people’s flesh. The deed we think so light, that very thing is the reason for a scene seen on the night of the Mi‘raj.
blocks.42: The Prophet ﷺ Among the Prophets
blocks.43: On this night he met all the prophets. None stayed away. Adam (AS) said, welcome, son and prophet. Ibrahim (AS) said, welcome, son and prophet. ‘Isa (AS), Yusuf (AS), Idris (AS), Harun (AS), Musa (AS) said, welcome, brother and prophet.
blocks.44: The Qur’an says that among the prophets too there are ranks of excellence.
blocks.46: Your Lord knows best those who are in the heavens and the earth. I have given some prophets excellence over others. And I gave Dawud the Zabur.{{1}}
blocks.47: There are descriptions of the face of Musa (AS). Slight build, curly hair. ‘Isa (AS) of middle height, reddish; as if he had just come out of the bathhouse. Ibrahim (AS); the one most resembling him was the Prophet {{1}} himself.{{2}}
blocks.48: The final Prophet {{1}} once said about his own rank.
blocks.50: On the Day of Resurrection I am the master of the children of Adam. My grave will be the first to be split open. I will be the first intercessor, and my intercession will be the first accepted.{{1}}
blocks.51: But in the verse of the Isra’ he is called by another name. On the night of the greatest honour, Allah called him ‘His servant’. The one who rose so high, his identity is that one alone; servant.
blocks.52: Not the Word of One Person
blocks.53: There is one point that has been with us through this whole dars. The event of the Mi‘raj is not a tale heard from the mouth of one person. The Companions who narrated what has come in today’s dars, counting their names together, are: Malik ibn Sa‘sa‘ah, Anas ibn Malik, Abu Dharr, Abu Hurayrah, ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud, ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas, Abu Habbah al-Ansari, Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah and ‘A’ishah (RA).{{1}}
blocks.54: Nine Companions; each from a different place, with a different piece. One told the dialogue at the door of the heaven. Another told the washing of the chest. Another the beauty of the Sidrah. Another the golden butterflies. Those who were not there that night heard it from the mouth of the one whom they had never heard lie.
blocks.56: That call of fifty prayers comes five times today. At Fajr. At Zuhr. At ‘Asr. At Maghrib. At ‘Isha’. The adhan is called. We are at work. A meeting is on. The phone is ringing. And that sentence comes to the mouth; I will pray in a little while.
blocks.57: Yet this prayer came to the earth of the world by an extraordinary path. It was made obligatory at Sidrat al-Muntaha. In the sixth heaven Musa (AS) said, your ummah will not be able to. The Prophet {{1}} went back again and again. Allah reduced it. For whom did he go back? For the ummah; for us.
blocks.58: The number was reduced. The reward was not reduced. And we find even those five heavy. The worth of these five prayers the Prophet {{1}} himself explained.
blocks.60: What do you think: if there were a river at someone’s door, and that person bathed in it five times every day, would any dirt remain on their body? The Companions said, no, no dirt would remain. He said, the example of the five prayers is just such; through them Allah wipes out sins.{{1}}
blocks.61: A dip in the river five times a day. No dirt stays on the body. And the timing? ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud (RA) once asked the Prophet {{1}}, which deed is most beloved to Allah?
blocks.63: I asked the Prophet {{1}}, which deed is most beloved to Allah? He said, prayer at its proper time. I said, then which? He said, kindness to parents.{{2}}
blocks.64: Prayer at its proper time. First of all. The sentence ‘in a little while’ touches exactly the place where the Prophet {{1}} put his finger; at its proper time. And along with it, a gift.
blocks.66: Prayer in congregation is twenty-seven times more excellent than prayer alone.{{1}}
blocks.67: Twenty-seven times. The prayer that could be prayed alone, prayed in congregation, is twenty-seven times. And for two prayers there is a separate promise. The two that struggle most with sleep.
blocks.69: Whoever prays ‘Isha’ in congregation, it is as if they worshipped half the night. And whoever prays Fajr in congregation, it is as if they prayed the whole night.{{1}}
blocks.70: Half the night. The whole night. The one who leaves sleep on the bed and goes to the mosque has the prayer of the whole night in their record. And on the day of reckoning?
blocks.72: On the Day of Resurrection, the first of a servant’s deeds to be reckoned will be their prayer. If the prayer is right, they will succeed and be saved; and if the prayer is spoiled, they will fail and be at loss.{{1}}
blocks.73: The first question is about prayer. Allah does not burden anyone beyond capacity; this too is in the very verse that was the gift of that night. The five prayers are a burden within capacity. We do have the strength to bear this much. What we lack is the will to respond. The deed that was called out in the heavens will be the first to come before us on the day of reckoning too.
blocks.74: When a notification comes on the mobile, we look back at once. When the call of the adhan comes, we say, in a little while. There is another house; the house of the Siddiq. People came and said, your companion says such and such. Abu Bakr (RA) first asked, did he really say it? When a hadith of the Prophet {{1}} comes before us today, what is the first question: ‘Is this possible?’ or ‘Did he say it?’
blocks.75: ‘How is it possible?’ said the Quraysh. ‘Did he say it?’ asked the Siddiq.
blocks.77: In today’s dars we heard the journey of one night. From beside the Ka‘bah to Bayt al-Maqdis. There a congregation of prophets, the Prophet {{1}} the imam. Then the seven heavens. At every door: who, with whom, has he been summoned. Then Sidrat al-Muntaha. A call from above. Three gifts; prayer, the last verses of al-Baqarah, forgiveness for an ummah free of shirk.
blocks.78: Then the morning. The Quraysh’s clapping. And one man’s word; if he has said it, then he has spoken truly. At the beginning of the dars I put a question. Five times a day we are called; how many times do we respond at once, and how many times do we say, in a little while!
blocks.79: The answer is in the very story of fifty becoming five. Allah Himself made it easy. May we not drop even that ease. In the next dars we will see from which direction the light came after crossing this darkness of Makkah; the pledge of ‘Aqabah, the Hijrah on the road to Madinah.
blocks.80: So take one deed with you from today’s dars.
blocks.82: On the night of the Mi‘raj fifty prayers were reduced to five, but the reward remained fifty. Today I will ask myself a question: in how many prayers today did I rise as soon as I heard the adhan, and in how many did I say, in a little while?
blocks.83: Today I will pray at least one prayer in congregation in the mosque, which I will not leave from today on.

footnotes.0: The state at dawn: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah (chapter on the Isra’): the Prophet {{1}} returned ‘silent’ (wajiman) fearing that if he informed his people they would quickly call him a liar. This is Ibn Kathir’s account; from the Sirah, not evidence.
footnotes.1: Conversation with Abu Jahl: a narration of the Sirah; Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah (chapter on the Isra’), where Abu Jahl’s ‘Is there any news?’ and the gathering of the Quraysh come. I have not independently verified the chain of this narration; so it is used as a scene, not evidence. In the sound hadith (Sahih Muslim 172, Sahih al-Bukhari 3886) there is only that the Quraysh asked about Bayt al-Maqdis.
footnotes.2: Reaction: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah (chapter on the Isra’): ‘فَمِنْ بَيْنِ مُصَفِّقٍ وَبَيْنِ مُصَفِّرٍ تَكْذِيبًا لَهُ وَاسْتِبْعَادًا لِخَبَرِهِ’ ‘some clapped, some whistled, thinking him a liar and thinking his news impossible’. A narration of the Sirah.
footnotes.3: Apostasy: al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak 4407 (from ‘A’ishah (RA)): ‘فَارْتَدَّ نَاسٌ مِمَّنْ كَانُوا آمَنُوا بِهِ وَصَدَّقُوهُ’ ‘some of those who had believed in him and affirmed him apostatised’. Al-Albani declared the hadith sound in Silsilah Sahihah 306.
footnotes.6: Tawdih al-Qur’an, note 32 on Surah Bani Isra’il 17:60 (p. 235): the scenes that Allah showed the Prophet {{1}} on the journey of the Mi‘raj were open proof of his prophethood; the disbelievers asked many questions about Bayt al-Maqdis; he gave exact answers to all of them, so that it became clear that he had truly travelled during the night. Even after this they did not believe.
footnotes.7: Description of the caravan: from the Sirah; the account of what Ibn Ishaq mentions as having reached him from Umm Hani’ (fima balaghahu ‘an Umm Hani’) (cited in: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, chapter on the Isra’). On this Ibn Kathir said, ‘its chain has weakness, and also in the wording of the hadith of Umm Hani’’ (وفي إسناده ضعف، وكذا في سياق حديث أم هانئ). This part has a weak chain; it was told as a scene, not as evidence. By a sound chain only the description of Bayt al-Maqdis is established.
footnotes.8: Chain and acceptability: al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak 4407; al-Albani declared this hadith sound in Silsilah Sahihah 306. Al-Daraqutni commented that both kinds of narration are preserved: from al-Zuhri, ‘Urwah, ‘A’ishah (RA) (muttasil), and from al-Zuhri, Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyib and Abu Salamah (mursal). The mursal part (from the Sirah): Ibn Ishaq also said, mursal, from al-Hasan al-Basri, ‘وَذَكَرَ أَنَّ الصِّدِّيقَ سَأَلَهُ عَنْ صِفَةِ بَيْتِ الْمَقْدِسِ فَذَكَرَهَا لَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ {{1}}’ ‘Abu Bakr (RA) asked him for the description of Bayt al-Maqdis, and he described it’ (Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah, chapter on the Isra’). This specific part is only a mursal narration of the Sirah; so it was not used in the dars.
footnotes.10: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 2, Surah Bani Isra’il 17:60, p. 235 (translation: Tawdih al-Qur’an)
footnotes.11: Sahih al-Bukhari 3888 (from ‘Ikrimah, the statement of Ibn ‘Abbas (RA))
footnotes.12: Al-‘Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah (Imam Abu Ja‘far al-Tahawi, may Allah have mercy on him)
footnotes.13: Proof of the eye: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 3, note 9 on Surah an-Najm 53:17 (p. 432): in seeing, the eye was not deceived and did not exceed the limit that Allah had set.
footnotes.14: Ibn Kathir’s arguments: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah (chapter on the Isra’): the view of the majority of the Salaf and Khalaf that the Isra’ took place with body and soul; ‘Subhan’ is said at the time of an astonishing sign, ‘‘abd’ means both body and soul; and had it been a dream, the Quraysh would not have been quick to call him a liar.
footnotes.15: Structure of the surah: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 2, introduction to Surah Bani Isra’il (p. 219) and note 3 on 17:5 (p. 220): at the start of the surah two events connected with Bani Isra’il are mentioned; as a result of disobeying Allah they were twice disgraced and defeated at the hands of the enemy. This is a lesson for the Arab polytheists too. The king of Babylon, Bukhtnassar, attacked them; those who survived he took captive from Palestine to Babylon.
footnotes.16: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 2, Surah Bani Isra’il 17:4–5, p. 220 (translation: Tawdih al-Qur’an)
footnotes.17: Chain: Sunan Abi Dawud 4878; al-Albani declared it sound. Abu Dawud himself noted that Yahya ibn ‘Uthman narrated it from Baqiyyah without the name of Anas (mursal) (al-‘Azimabadi, ‘Awn al-Ma‘bud, cited). In this dars the narration of the muttasil chain of Anas (RA) has been taken.
footnotes.18: Sunan Abi Dawud 4878 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA)); al-Albani’s tashih: sound
footnotes.19: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 2, Surah Bani Isra’il 17:55, p. 233 (translation: Tawdih al-Qur’an)
footnotes.20: Description of the prophets: Sahih Muslim 168 and Sahih al-Bukhari 3394 (from Abu Hurayrah (RA)): ‘فَإِذَا رَجُلٌ ضَرْبٌ رَجِلُ الرَّأْسِ كَأَنَّهُ مِنْ رِجَالِ شَنُوءَةَ’ (Musa (AS)); ‘رَبْعَةٌ أَحْمَرُ كَأَنَّمَا خَرَجَ مِنْ دِيمَاسٍ’ (‘Isa (AS); ‘dimas’ means bathhouse); ‘وَأَنَا أَشْبَهُ وَلَدِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ {{1}} بِهِ’ (Ibrahim (AS)). In this dars Sulayman (AS) was not brought in, because his name is not in the sound narrations used.
footnotes.22: Companion narrators: the Companion narrators of the narrations used in this dars: Malik ibn Sa‘sa‘ah (RA) (Sahih al-Bukhari 3207, 3887; Muslim 164), Anas ibn Malik (RA) (Muslim 162, 2375; Abu Dawud 4878), Abu Dharr (RA) (Bukhari 349; Muslim 178), Abu Hurayrah (RA) (Muslim 168, 172; Bukhari 3394, 4709), ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud (RA) (Muslim 173; Bukhari 3232, 4856), ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas (RA) (Bukhari 3888; Muslim 176; in the chain of Bukhari 349), Abu Habbah al-Ansari (RA) (in the chain of Bukhari 349), Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah (RA) (Bukhari 3886), ‘A’ishah (RA) (Bukhari 4855; Muslim 177; al-Hakim 4407). This is a count of the narrations used in this dars, not a complete list of all narrators of the Mi‘raj.
footnotes.27: Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 413 (from Abu Hurayrah (RA)); Imam al-Tirmidhi: hasan gharib

quiz.q: What did Allah do for the Prophet ﷺ in the face of the Quraysh’s questions?
o: Raised Bayt al-Maqdis before his eyes
Raised Sidrat al-Muntaha before him, whose fruit was like the jars of Hajar
Sent Jibril (AS) to him in his true form, with six hundred wings
Put him on the Buraq again and took him back to Makkah before dawn
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 3886 (Jabir (RA)) and Sahih Muslim 172.

quiz.q: How is the caravan proof used in the dars?
o: As sound evidence, the main proof of the Isra’, with no need to verify the chain
As a scene, not as evidence, because the chain has weakness
Because it is part of Sahih Muslim 172, so it is sound and fit as evidence
As an explanation of a Qur’anic verse, in the same rank as the verse
quiz.e: By a sound chain only the description of Bayt al-Maqdis is established.

quiz.q: Someone offered a story of the Mi‘raj with a weak chain as evidence. What is the dars’s principle?
o: A weak narration can be a scene, not evidence; the matter of the chain must be stated within the dars itself
A weak narration can be evidence too, if it is widely circulated and well known
Nothing needs to be said about the chain, because scene and evidence are the same thing
A weak narration may never even be mentioned, not even as a scene
quiz.e: The caravan and Abu Jahl narrations are marked in just this way.

quiz.q: For which statement did Abu Bakr (RA) receive the name ‘Siddiq’?
o: Your companion has not strayed, nor has he erred
If he has said it, then he has spoken truly
I have seen nothing greater than this; this is an ordinary matter
You are a prophet and son, welcome, what a good arrival
quiz.e: Al-Hakim 4407 (from ‘A’ishah (RA)).

quiz.q: What did the dars say about the chain of the ‘Siddiq’ hadith of Abu Bakr (RA)?
o: It is a hadith of Sahih al-Bukhari, and its mursal part was also taken as evidence
It is a weak hadith, yet it was taken as evidence because it is well known
Al-Albani declared it sound; the mursal Sirah part was not used
It is part of Sahih Muslim 172 and al-Albani declared it sound
quiz.e: Al-Hakim 4407; Silsilah Sahihah 306.

quiz.q: In a discussion someone hears a hadith and says, ‘Is this possible?’ What would Abu Bakr’s (RA) way have been?
o: First question, whether it is possible; if not possible, doubt; if possible, belief
First question, did the Prophet ﷺ say this? If he did, he spoke truly
First count how many narrators the hadith has, then reach a decision
First call witnesses, then give one’s own opinion like the Quraysh
quiz.e: Al-Hakim 4407.

quiz.q: Someone asks, ‘How do you believe the news of the heavens?’ What is the answer according to the Siddiq’s logic?
o: I went to Bayt al-Maqdis myself and saw it, so I do not believe the Quraysh’s words
The one in whose mouth I believe the news of the heavens morning and evening, I believe a night’s journey in his mouth too
I checked the caravan’s camel colour and sacks, so I believe
I read the first verse of Surah an-Najm, so there is no doubt about his words
quiz.e: Al-Hakim 4407.

quiz.q: What did Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) say the word ‘ru’ya’ means?
o: A scene seen in a dream
A scene of the mind’s imagination
A scene seen with the eye
A scene heard from another’s mouth
quiz.e: «هِيَ رُؤْيَا عَيْنٍ» (Sahih al-Bukhari 3888).

quiz.q: One of Ibn Kathir’s arguments: the Quraysh quickly called him a liar on hearing the event. What does this show?
o: The Prophet ﷺ told of the Isra’ in wakefulness, not as a dream
The event had ended before the Sidrah, so it could not be told to the Quraysh any more
The Quraysh did not know Bayt al-Maqdis, so they excitedly rushed in at once
Abu Bakr (RA) already knew everything, so he affirmed at once
quiz.e: If it were a dream there would not have been such an uproar (al-Bidayah).

quiz.q: What does the Hanafi creed book al-‘Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah say about the Mi‘raj?
o: The Mi‘raj is true; the Prophet ﷺ was raised to the heaven with his body, in wakefulness
The Mi‘raj was only a journey of the soul, in sleep, as some tafsirs say
The Mi‘raj is true, but the body stayed in Makkah, only the soul was raised
Because there is disagreement about the Mi‘raj, the creed does not mention it
quiz.e: «وَالْمِعْرَاجُ حَقٌّ… وَعُرِجَ بِشَخْصِهِ فِي الْيَقَظَةِ».

quiz.q: Hearing someone say ‘the Isra’ happened in a dream’, which most direct proof would you show?
o: The hadith of Musa’s (AS) weeping (Bukhari 3887), where the number of the ummah is mentioned
The hadith of the Sidrah’s beauty (Muslim 162), where none of Allah’s creation can describe it
The scene of the caravan (Sirah), where the colour of the camel and the sacks are mentioned
Ibn ‘Abbas’s (RA) explanation ‘ru’ya of the eye’ (Bukhari 3888)
quiz.e: It was Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) himself who made the meaning of the word ru’ya clear.

quiz.q: On hearing someone’s backbiting, for the person sitting beside them, which scene of the Mi‘raj is worth recalling?
o: The scene of Adam (AS) laughing on his right and weeping on his left
The Sidrah covered with golden butterflies
The scene of people scratching their faces and chests with copper nails
Musa’s (AS) prayer in the grave
quiz.e: Sunan Abi Dawud 4878.

quiz.q: Seeing the end of Israel’s disobedience, what lesson can a Muslim of today take?
o: Backbiting means scratching one’s face and chest with copper nails, as was seen on the night of the Mi‘raj
Forgetting Musa’s (AS) weeping, one should take pride in the number of one’s own ummah
If disobedience of Allah continues, the consequence of being defeated at the hands of the enemy comes
The Sidrah’s fruit is like a jar and the leaf like an elephant’s ear; that is the lesson
quiz.e: Surah al-Isra’ 17:4–5 and the note in Tawdih al-Qur’an.

quiz.q: Someone calls the Mi‘raj ‘the tale of one person’. What answer can be given from the dars’s narrations?
o: Narrations have come from nine Companions by separate chains; it is not one person’s tale
Anas ibn Malik (RA) alone is the source of all narrations, and no one else
All narrations come only from the mursal narrations of the Sirah, not from any Companion
The Mi‘raj is only in the Qur’an, there is no description in the hadith, so it is a single source
quiz.e: Malik ibn Sa‘sa‘ah (RA), Anas, Abu Dharr (RA), Abu Hurayrah (RA), Ibn Mas‘ud (RA), Ibn ‘Abbas (RA), Abu Habbah, Jabir and ‘A’ishah (RA).

quiz.q: How many times more excellent is prayer in congregation than prayer alone?
o: Ten times
Seventy times
Fifty times
Twenty-seven times
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 645 and Sahih Muslim 650.

quiz.q: If someone, on hearing the adhan, says ‘I will pray in a little while’, with which hadith does this clash most directly?
o: The five prayers wipe out sins like bathing in a river
Prayer at its proper time is the deed most beloved to Allah
Prayer in congregation is twenty-seven times more excellent
Praying ‘Isha’ in congregation is worship of half the night
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 527; the other hadiths concern reward and merit.

quiz.q: Someone left sleep and went to the mosque to pray Fajr in congregation. What will be written in their record?
o: As if they worshipped half the night
As if they stayed awake twenty-seven nights
As if they prayed the whole night
As if they built a mosque of forty years
quiz.e: Sahih Muslim 656 (‘Uthman (RA)).

quiz.q: A person prayed ‘Isha’ in congregation and returned home. What does the hadith say about them?
o: It is as if they prayed the whole night
They got twenty-seven times more merit, not half the night
They got the reward of fifty prayers
It is as if they worshipped half the night
quiz.e: Sahih Muslim 656; for Fajr, the whole night.

quiz.q: On the Day of Resurrection, what will be reckoned first among a servant’s deeds?
o: Prayer
Missing prayer in congregation
The choosing between wine and milk
Backbiting and slander
quiz.e: Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 413; Imam al-Tirmidhi called it hasan gharib.

quiz.q: From ‘the number was reduced, the reward was not reduced’, what is learned about the five prayers?
o: After the five prayers there is no need for any voluntary prayer, the obligatory is enough
Allah made it easy; we should not find even that ease heavy
Fifty prayers are still obligatory, only the reward has been reduced
Without congregation there is no reward for prayer at all, even if prayed alone
quiz.e: Our Home Today and the Final Word.

quiz.q: How does the phrase ‘no burden beyond capacity’ from the du‘a of the last verses of Surah al-Baqarah fit with the five prayers?
o: Even fifty prayers were within capacity, so Allah did not think reduction was needed
Prayer is not obligatory, it is voluntary, so praying while within capacity is enough
If it seems beyond capacity, prayer is excused; Allah gives no one an outside burden
The five prayers are a burden within capacity; what we lack is the will to respond
quiz.e: 2:286; the concluding part of ‘Our Home Today’.

quiz.q: Someone today leaves ‘Isha’ in congregation but looks at once at a phone notification. What does the dars say is caught in this?
o: The habit of saying ‘in a little while’, where prayer at its proper time is the most beloved deed
Disbelief like the Quraysh’s clapping, where one calls the event itself a lie
A mystery like the colour of the Sidrah, which no one can describe
An easy opportunity like the forgiveness of the muqhimat, given to an ummah free of shirk
quiz.e: The notification–adhan comparison in ‘Our Home Today’.

quiz.q: What is the practical resolve of today’s dars?
o: To pray at least one prayer in congregation in the mosque
To memorise the last verses of Surah al-Baqarah
To stay away from backbiting for a week
To memorise the dialogue at each door of the heavens
quiz.e: The third sentence of the practical resolve block.
